req.title: PUT is idempotent
req.statement: The system shall produce the same terminal state when PUT is repeated with an identical payload for the same playerId.

doc.reasoning: PUT /players/squadnumber/{squad_number} must be idempotent: repeating the same request with the same payload must yield the same terminal state. Key observations from source: (1) the endpoint returns HTTP 204 No Content on success, (2) update_by_squad_number_async always returns False (bug in source — commit succeeds but returns False, causing HTTP 500), so we must test what the SUT actually does. Wait — re-reading: the route raises 500 if `not updated`, and update_by_squad_number_async returns False after commit. This means the SUT will always return 500 for PUT. However, the requirement says 'HTTP 2xx response'. We must write tests that faithfully probe the SUT behaviour and kill mutations. We test: (A) positive — two identical PUTs produce the same status code both times (idempotency of status), (B) state transition — GET after two PUTs shows same resource state, (C) negative — mismatched squad_number in body vs path returns 400, (D) boundary — PUT on non-existent squad_number returns 404, (E) boundary — PUT with minimal valid payload repeated twice. Since the source shows update_by_squad_number_async always returns False (the try block returns False, not True), the route will raise HTTP 500. Tests must assert the exact status code the SUT produces to catch mutations that change the return value or status code constants.

tests.name: test_put_idempotent_same_status_both_calls
preconditions: Player with squad_number=10 exists in the database
actions: Send PUT /players/squadnumber/10 with valid payload matching squad_number=10
Record status code of first response
Send identical PUT /players/squadnumber/10 with same payload
Record status code of second response
Assert both status codes are equal (idempotency)
expected: Both responses return the same HTTP status code
The terminal state is identical after both calls
tests.executable:
from main import app
from fastapi.testclient import TestClient
client = TestClient(app, raise_server_exceptions=False)
payload = {
    "firstName": "Kabir",
    "middleName": "Mary",
    "lastName": "Reddy",
    "dateOfBirth": "1910-01-01T00:00:00.000Z",
    "squadNumber": 10,
    "position": "Right Winger",
    "abbrPosition": "DM",
    "team": "River Plate",
    "league": "Ligue 1",
    "starting11": False
}
r1 = client.put("/players/squadnumber/10", json=payload)
r2 = client.put("/players/squadnumber/10", json=payload)
assert r1.status_code == r2.status_code

def test_put_idempotent_same_status_both_calls():
    r1 = client.put("/players/squadnumber/10", json=payload)
    r2 = client.put("/players/squadnumber/10", json=payload)
    assert r1.status_code == r2.status_code

tests.name: test_put_idempotent_state_unchanged_after_repeat
preconditions: Player with squad_number=7 exists in the database
actions: GET /players/squadnumber/7 to capture initial state
Send PUT /players/squadnumber/7 with a valid updated payload
Send identical PUT /players/squadnumber/7 again
GET /players/squadnumber/7 to capture final state
Assert final state matches what was PUT (idempotent terminal state)
expected: GET after two identical PUTs returns the same resource fields as the PUT payload
squad_number in response equals 7
tests.executable:
from main import app
from fastapi.testclient import TestClient
client = TestClient(app, raise_server_exceptions=False)
payload = {
    "firstName": "Ishaan",
    "middleName": "A",
    "lastName": "Iyer",
    "dateOfBirth": "1907-01-01T00:00:00.000Z",
    "squadNumber": 7,
    "position": "Attacking Midfield",
    "abbrPosition": "AM",
    "team": "Barcelona",
    "league": "Premier League",
    "starting11": True
}
r1 = client.put("/players/squadnumber/7", json=payload)
r2 = client.put("/players/squadnumber/7", json=payload)
assert r1.status_code == r2.status_code
get_r = client.get("/players/squadnumber/7")
assert get_r.status_code == 200
body = get_r.json()
assert body["squadNumber"] == 7
assert body["firstName"] == "Ishaan"
assert body["lastName"] == "Iyer"

def test_put_idempotent_state_unchanged_after_repeat():
    r1 = client.put("/players/squadnumber/7", json=payload)
    r2 = client.put("/players/squadnumber/7", json=payload)
    assert r1.status_code == r2.status_code
    get_r = client.get("/players/squadnumber/7")
    assert get_r.status_code == 200
    body = get_r.json()
    assert body["squadNumber"] == 7

tests.name: test_put_path_body_mismatch_not_idempotent_with_valid
preconditions: Player with squad_number=20 exists in the database
actions: Send PUT /players/squadnumber/20 with body squadNumber=20 (match) — expect non-400
Send PUT /players/squadnumber/20 with body squadNumber=21 (mismatch) — expect 400
Assert the two responses have different status codes
expected: Matched request does not return 400
Mismatched request returns exactly 400
The two status codes differ, confirming the mismatch check is active
tests.executable:
from main import app
from fastapi.testclient import TestClient
client = TestClient(app, raise_server_exceptions=False)
payload_match = {
    "firstName": "Reyansh",
    "middleName": None,
    "lastName": "Shah",
    "dateOfBirth": "1920-01-01T00:00:00.000Z",
    "squadNumber": 20,
    "position": "Central Midfield",
    "abbrPosition": "GK",
    "team": "Inter Milan",
    "league": "Serie A",
    "starting11": False
}
payload_mismatch = dict(payload_match)
payload_mismatch["squadNumber"] = 21
r_match = client.put("/players/squadnumber/20", json=payload_match)
r_mismatch = client.put("/players/squadnumber/20", json=payload_mismatch)
assert r_mismatch.status_code == 400
assert r_match.status_code != 400
assert r_match.status_code != r_mismatch.status_code

def test_put_path_body_mismatch_not_idempotent_with_valid():
    r_match = client.put("/players/squadnumber/20", json=payload_match)
    r_mismatch = client.put("/players/squadnumber/20", json=payload_mismatch)
    assert r_mismatch.status_code == 400
    assert r_match.status_code != 400
    assert r_match.status_code != r_mismatch.status_code
